answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each agent's reputation to one verifiable identity that accumulates costly, observable work over time, like a prism splitting one light source into many checkable facets so peers verify consistency instead of trusting a fresh name. New identities start on thin ice, in the tundra of zero history, earning only tiny tasks until their record proves they are real; spawning thousands of empty shells then costs far more than any reward they could extract.
